units.zh: 劉鍾崔二王
units.en: Liu, Zhong, Cui, and the two Wangs
units.literal: Liu, Zhong, Cui, and the two Wangs

units.zh: ◎劉鐘崔二王
units.en: ◎ Liu, Zhong, Cui, and the two Wangs
units.literal: ◎ Liu, Zhong, Cui, and the two Wangs

units.zh: 劉幽求，冀州武強人。
units.en: Liu Youqiu came from Wuqiang in Jizhou.
units.literal: Liu Youqiu was a native of Wuqiang in Jizhou.

units.zh: 聖歷中，舉制科中第。
units.en: During the Shengli reign he passed the special civil-service examination.
units.literal: During the Shengli era he passed the special examination.

units.zh: 調閬中尉，刺史不禮，棄官去。
units.en: Appointed magistrate of Langzhong, he quit when the prefect refused him proper respect.
units.literal: He was assigned as magistrate of Langzhong; the prefect did not treat him with courtesy, and he abandoned his post and left.

units.zh: 久之，授朝邑尉。
units.en: Some time later he received an appointment as assistant magistrate of Chaoyi.
units.literal: After a long while he was appointed assistant magistrate of Chaoyi.

units.zh: 桓彥範等誅張易之、昌宗，而不殺武三思，幽求謂彥範曰：「公等無葬地矣。
units.en: After Huan Yanfan and his allies killed Zhang Yizhi and Changzong but spared Wu Sansi, Youqiu warned Yanfan, "You will leave yourselves no ground for a grave.
units.literal: When Huan Yanfan and the others executed Zhang Yizhi and Changzong but did not kill Wu Sansi, Youqiu said to Yanfan, "You gentlemen will have no place for burial.

units.zh: 不早計，後且噬臍。」
units.en: Unless you act now, you will regret it too late to help yourselves."
units.literal: If you do not plan early, later you will bite your navel in regret."

units.zh: 不從。
units.en: They paid him no heed.
units.literal: They did not heed him.

units.zh: 既，五王皆為三思構死。
units.en: Before long all five princes had been destroyed through Sansi's machinations.
units.literal: Afterward the Five Princes were all framed and put to death by Sansi.

units.zh: 臨淄王入誅韋庶人，預參大策，是夜號令詔敕一出其手。
units.en: When the Prince of Linzi marched in to destroy Consort Wei, Youqiu helped shape the coup; that night every command and proclamation bore his hand.
units.literal: When the Prince of Linzi entered the capital to execute the Deposed Consort Wei, Youqiu took part in the great plan; that night every order and edict issued from his hand alone.

units.zh: 以功授中書舍人，參知機務，爵中山縣男，實封二百戶，授二子五品官，二代俱贈刺史。
units.en: Rewarded with the post of Secretariat Drafter and a share in governing, he was created Baron of Zhongshan with two hundred taxable households, his two sons were granted fifth-rank posts, and his forebears for two generations were posthumously made prefects.
units.literal: For his merit he was made Secretariat Drafter, with a role in state affairs; he was ennobled as Baron of Zhongshan with a substantive fief of two hundred households; his two sons were given fifth-rank offices, and both generations of forebears were posthumously honored as prefects.

units.zh: 睿宗立，進尚書右丞、徐國公，增封戶至五百，賜物千段、奴婢二十人、第一區、良田千畝、金銀雜物稱是。
units.en: After Ruizong's accession he rose to Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Duke of Xu, his fief was raised to five hundred households, and he received a thousand lengths of silk, twenty servants, a mansion, a thousand mu of fertile land, and commensurate gold and silver.
units.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, Youqiu was promoted to Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and made Duke of Xu, with his fief increased to five hundred households; he was given a thousand lengths of goods, twenty slaves, one fine residence, a thousand mu of good land, and gold, silver, and other valuables in proportion.

units.zh: 景雲二年，以戶部尚書罷政事。
units.en: In Jingyun 2 he left office while serving as Minister of Revenue.
units.literal: In the second year of Jingyun he left the government as Minister of Revenue.

units.zh: 不旬月，遷吏部，拜侍中。
units.en: In less than a month he moved to the Ministry of Personnel and was made Palace Attendant.
units.literal: Within less than ten days he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel and appointed Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 璽詔曰：「頃王室不造，中宗厭代，戚孽專亂，將隕社稷，朕與王公皆幾於難。
units.en: An imperial edict declared: "The house has lately been afflicted: Zhongzong left the throne, vicious relatives seized power and nearly destroyed the realm, and I with the princes and officials were all but undone.
units.literal: An imperial edict said: "Recently the royal house suffered misfortune; Emperor Zhongzong passed from the throne; wicked kin monopolized rebellion and nearly brought down the altars of state; I and the princes and ministers all came close to ruin.

units.zh: 幽求處危思奮，翊贊聖儲，協和義士，震殄元惡。
units.en: Youqiu rose to the crisis, backed the rightful heir, rallied loyal men, and crushed the arch-villains.
units.literal: Youqiu, facing peril, thought to strive; he aided and supported the sacred heir, united men of righteousness, and in awe struck down the chief evil.

units.zh: 國家之復存，繄幽求是賴，厥庸茂焉，朕用嘉之。
units.en: The realm's survival rested on Youqiu; his service was great, and I honor it accordingly.
units.literal: That the state was restored to life depended on Youqiu; his merit is abundant, and I therefore praise him.

units.zh: 雖胙以土宇，而賦入未廣。
units.en: Though he has been granted a fief, its revenue remains modest.
units.literal: Although enfeoffed with territory, his tax income is not yet broad.

units.zh: 昔西漢行封，更擇多戶；
units.en: In the Western Han, new enfeoffments were often drawn from more populous districts;
units.literal: Formerly in the Western Han, when enfeoffments were granted, households of greater number were chosen again;

units.zh: 東京定賞，復增大邑。
units.en: and when rewards were fixed in the Eastern Capital, large fiefs were again enlarged.
units.literal: in the Eastern Capital when rewards were fixed, great districts were again enlarged.

units.zh: 宜加賜實封二百戶，子子孫孫傳國無絕，特免十死，銘諸鐵券，以傳其功。」
units.en: Let an additional two hundred taxable households be granted, the fief to pass in perpetuity, ten capital offenses remitted, and the deed engraved on an iron charter so his service may endure."
units.literal: He should be further granted two hundred households of substantive fief, with the state transmitted without end from sons to grandsons; he is specially exempted from ten deaths; this shall be inscribed on the iron certificate to transmit his merit."

units.zh: 先天元年，為尚書右仆射、同中書門下三品，監修國史。
units.en: In Xiantian 1 he was made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, a participant in the highest council, and put in charge of compiling the national history.
units.literal: In the first year of Xiantian he became Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, with the same rank as the Three Departments at the Secretariat Chancellery, and supervised compilation of the national history.

units.zh: 幽求自謂有勞於國，在諸臣右，意望未滿，而竇懷貞為左仆射，崔湜為中書令，殊不平，見於言面。
units.en: Youqiu believed his service outranked every other minister and resented that Dou Huaizhen held the left vice-directorship and Cui Shi the directorship of the Secretariat; his discontent showed plainly in word and face.
units.literal: Youqiu considered that he had labored for the state and stood above the other ministers; his ambitions were not satisfied, yet Dou Huaizhen was Left Vice Director and Cui Shi was Director of the Secretariat—he was deeply displeased, and it showed in his speech and countenance.

units.zh: 已而湜等附太平公主，有逆計。
units.en: Soon Shi and his circle aligned with Princess Taiping and plotted rebellion.
units.literal: Before long Shi and the others attached themselves to Princess Taiping and had a treasonous design.

units.zh: 幽求與右羽林將軍張暐定計，使暐說玄宗曰：「湜等皆太平黨與，日夜陰計，若不早圖，且產大害，太上不得高枕矣。
units.en: Youqiu and Zhang Wei of the Right Imperial Insignia Army laid a plan whereby Wei urged Xuanzong: "Shi and his allies are Princess Taiping's faction, scheming night and day; unless you strike first, grave harm will follow and your father will never sleep in peace.
units.literal: Youqiu with the Right General of the Imperial Insignia Army Zhang Wei formed a plan and had Wei persuade Emperor Xuanzong, saying, "Shi and the rest are all partisans of Taiping, plotting day and night in secret; if we do not act early, great harm will soon arise, and the Retired Emperor will not be able to rest easy.

units.zh: 臣請督羽林兵除之。」
units.en: I beg leave to command the palace guard and destroy them."
units.literal: Your subject asks to lead the Imperial Insignia troops to eliminate them."

units.zh: 帝許之。
units.en: The emperor agreed.
units.literal: The Emperor consented.

units.zh: 未發也，而暐漏言於侍御史鄧光賓，帝懼，即列其狀。
units.en: Before they could act, Wei let the plan slip to Censor Deng Guangbin; alarmed, the emperor reported the whole affair himself.
units.literal: Before it was launched, Wei leaked word to Attending Censor Deng Guangbin; the Emperor feared exposure and at once set forth the facts.

units.zh: 睿宗以幽求等屬吏，劾奏以疏間親，罪應死。
units.en: Ruizong turned Youqiu and his associates over for trial; they were charged with driving a wedge between father and son, a crime punishable by death.
units.literal: Ruizong handed Youqiu and the others over to the officials, who memorialized that by estranging kin they had committed a capital offense.

units.zh: 帝密申右之，乃流幽求於封州、暐於峰州、光賓於繡州。
units.en: The emperor intervened in secret, and the sentences were commuted to exile: Youqiu to Feng, Wei to Peak, and Guangbin to Xiu.
units.literal: The Emperor secretly pleaded on their behalf, and they were banished—Youqiu to Fengzhou, Wei to Peak Prefecture (Fengzhou), and Guangbin to Xiuzhou.

units.zh: 明年，太平公主誅，即日召復舊官，知軍國事，還封戶，賜錦衣一襲。
units.en: The following year, after Princess Taiping was killed, he was recalled the same day to his old post, entrusted with military and civil affairs, had his fief restored, and received a brocade robe.
units.literal: The next year, when Princess Taiping was executed, he was summoned the same day to his former office, placed in charge of military and state affairs, had his fief households restored, and was given one suit of brocade robes.

units.zh: 開元初，進尚書左丞相，兼黃門監，俄以太子少保罷。
units.en: Early in Kaiyuan he rose to Left Director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrent Supervisor of the Yellow Gate, but soon left office as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
units.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan he was advanced to Left Director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrently Supervisor of the Yellow Gate; soon he was dismissed as Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 姚崇素忌之，奏幽求郁怏散職，有怨言。
units.en: Yao Chong, who had long envied him, reported that Youqiu, bitter over a sinecure, was voicing grievances.
units.literal: Yao Chong had long resented him and memorialized that Youqiu, discontented in a loose post, uttered complaints.

units.zh: 詔有司鞫治，宰相盧懷慎等奏言：「幽求輕肆不恭，失大臣禮，乖崖分之節。」
units.en: The court was ordered to investigate; Chancellor Lu Huaishen and others reported, "Youqiu had been insolent and disrespectful, failing in a minister's decorum and overstepping his place."
units.literal: An edict ordered the authorities to investigate; the chief ministers Lu Huaishen and others memorialized, "Youqiu is frivolous and disrespectful, has lost the rites due a great minister, and violated the bounds of his station."

units.zh: 翌日，貶睦州刺史，削實封戶六百。
units.en: The next day he was demoted to prefect of Mu and lost six hundred fief households.
units.literal: The next day he was demoted to prefect of Muzhou and stripped of six hundred households of substantive fief.

units.zh: 遷杭、郴二州，恚憤卒於道，年六十一。
units.en: Reassigned through Hang and Chen, he died on the road in bitter anger at sixty-one.
units.literal: He was transferred through Hang and Chen prefectures and died on the road from resentment and anger, aged sixty-one.

units.zh: 贈禮部尚書，謚曰文獻。
units.en: He was posthumously honored as Minister of Rites with the title Wenxian (Cultivated and Meritorious).
units.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Rites, with the posthumous title Wenxian.

units.zh: 六年，詔與蘇瑰配享睿宗廟廷。
units.en: In the sixth year he was ordered to share offerings in Ruizong's temple alongside Su Gui.
units.literal: In the sixth year an edict ordered him to share sacrifice in Ruizong's temple court with Su Gui.

units.zh: 建中中，追贈司徒。
units.en: Under Jianzhong he was posthumously made Grand Mentor.
units.literal: During Jianzhong he was posthumously made Grand Mentor.

units.zh: 鐘紹京，虔州贛人。
units.en: Zhong Shaojing came from Gan in Qianzhou.
units.literal: Zhong Shaojing was a native of Gan in Qianzhou.

units.zh: 初為司農錄事，以善書直鳳閣。
units.en: He began as a clerk in the Ministry of Agriculture and, for his calligraphy, was posted to Phoenix Pavilion.
units.literal: At first he was a clerk in the Ministry of Agriculture; for skill in calligraphy he served directly at Phoenix Pavilion.

units.zh: 武後時署諸宮殿、明堂及銘九鼎，皆其筆也。
units.en: Under Empress Wu he wrote the inscriptions for the palaces, the Bright Hall, and the Nine Cauldrons.
units.literal: Under Empress Wu he inscribed the various palaces, the Bright Hall, and the inscriptions on the Nine Cauldrons—all were in his hand.

units.zh: 景龍中，為苑總監，會討韋氏難，紹京帥戶奴、丁夫從。
units.en: During Jinglong he directed the imperial parks; when forces moved against the Wei clan, he led household servants and laborers into the fight.
units.literal: In the Jinglong era he was Director of the Imperial Parks; when the campaign against the Wei faction arose, Shaojing led household slaves and corvée laborers to follow.

units.zh: 事平，夜拜中書侍郎，參知機務。
units.en: After victory he was named Vice Director of the Secretariat the same night and given a share in governing.
units.literal: When the affair was settled, that night he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat with a role in state affairs.

units.zh: 明日，進中書令、越國公，實封五百戶，賚賜與劉幽求等。
units.en: The next day he became Director of the Secretariat and Duke of Yue with five hundred fief households, receiving rewards equal to Liu Youqiu's.
units.literal: The next day he was advanced to Director of the Secretariat and Duke of Yue, with a substantive fief of five hundred households; gifts and rewards matched those of Liu Youqiu and the others.

units.zh: 既當路，以賞罰自肆，當時惡之。
units.en: In office he wielded rewards and punishments arbitrarily, and contemporaries loathed him for it.
units.literal: Once in power he indulged himself in rewards and punishments, and men of the time detested him.

units.zh: 因上疏讓官，睿宗用薛稷謀，進戶部尚書，出為彭州刺史。
units.en: He petitioned to resign; Ruizong, heeding Xue Ji, made him Minister of Revenue and then sent him out as prefect of Peng.
units.literal: He therefore submitted a memorial yielding his office; Ruizong followed Xue Ji's counsel, promoted him to Minister of Revenue, and sent him out as prefect of Pengzhou.

units.zh: 玄宗即位，復拜戶部尚書，增實封，改太子詹事。
units.en: At Xuanzong's accession he was again made Minister of Revenue, his fief was enlarged, and he was appointed Steward of the Heir Apparent.
units.literal: When Xuanzong took the throne, Shaojing was again appointed Minister of Revenue, his substantive fief was increased, and he was changed to Steward of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 不為姚祟所喜，與幽求並以怨望得罪，貶果州刺史，賜封邑百戶。
units.en: Disliked by Yao Chong, he and Youqiu were alike punished for discontent and demoted; Shaojing became prefect of Guo with a nominal fief of one hundred households.
units.literal: Not favored by Yao Chong, he and Youqiu alike were punished for resentful longing and demoted—Shaojing to prefect of Guozhou, with a fief district of one hundred households granted.

units.zh: 後坐它事，貶懷恩尉，悉奪階封，再遷溫州別駕。
units.en: Later, implicated in another case, he was reduced to assistant magistrate of Huai'en, stripped of rank and fief, and eventually made vice-prefect of Wen.
units.literal: Later, convicted on another matter, he was demoted to assistant magistrate of Huai'en; all ranks and fiefs were stripped, and he was transferred again to vice-prefect of Wenzhou.

units.zh: 十五年入朝，見帝泣曰：「陛下忘疇日事邪，忍使棄死草莽！
units.en: In the fifteenth year he appeared at court, wept before the emperor, and said, "Have you forgotten what we did together, that you would leave me to die forgotten in the weeds?
units.literal: In the fifteenth year he came to court, saw the Emperor, and weeping said, "Has Your Majesty forgotten affairs of former days, that you would bear to leave me to die abandoned in the wilds!

units.zh: 且同時立功者，今骨已朽，而獨臣在，陛下不垂湣乎？」
units.en: Of all who earned merit that day, only I still live while the rest are dust—will you not show me mercy?"
units.literal: Moreover, of those who achieved merit at the same time, their bones are now decayed, yet I alone remain—will Your Majesty not show pity?

units.zh: 帝惻然，即日授太子右諭德。
units.en: Moved, the emperor named him Right Admonisher to the Heir Apparent that very day.
units.literal: The Emperor was moved and that same day appointed him Right Admonisher of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 久之，遷少詹事。
units.en: Some time later he was made Junior Steward of the Heir Apparent.
units.literal: After a long while he was transferred to Junior Steward of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 年逾八十，以官壽卒。
units.en: He died in office past eighty, having completed his span in service.
units.literal: Past eighty years of age, he died in office of natural causes.

units.zh: 紹京嗜書畫，如王義之、獻之、褚遂良真跡，藏家者至數十百卷。
units.en: Shaojing loved calligraphy and painting; households that owned authentic pieces by Wang Xizhi, Wang Xianzhi, or Chu Suiliang might hold dozens or even hundreds of scrolls.
units.literal: Shaojing was fond of calligraphy and painting; authentic works of Wang Xizhi, Wang Xianzhi, and Chu Suiliang in collectors' homes might reach scores or hundreds of scrolls.

units.zh: 建中中，追贈太子太傅。
units.en: Under Jianzhong he was posthumously honored as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
units.literal: During Jianzhong he was posthumously made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 崔日用，滑州靈昌人。
units.en: Cui Riyong came from Lingchang in Hua Prefecture.
units.literal: Cui Riyong was a native of Lingchang in Hua Prefecture.

units.zh: 擢進士第，為芮城尉。
units.en: He passed the jinshi examination and became assistant magistrate of Ruicheng.
units.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed assistant magistrate of Ruicheng.

units.zh: 大足元年，武後幸長安，陜州刺史宗楚客委以頓峙，饋獻豐甘，稱過賓使者。
units.en: In Dazu 1, when Empress Wu visited Chang'an, Zong Chuke, prefect of Shan, put him in charge of provisioning the imperial progress; he supplied rich delicacies and surpassed the envoys of passing guests.
units.literal: In the first year of Dazu, when Empress Wu visited Chang'an, Zong Chuke, prefect of Shan Prefecture, entrusted him with provisioning the imperial progress; he presented abundant delicacies and outdid the envoys of passing guests.

units.zh: 楚客嘆其能，亟薦之，擢為新豐尉，遷監宗御史。
units.en: Chuke admired his talent, quickly recommended him, made him assistant magistrate of Xinfeng, and then transferred him to investigating censor of the Court of the Imperial Clan.
units.literal: Chuke marveled at his ability, urgently recommended him, promoted him to assistant magistrate of Xinfeng, and transferred him to investigating censor of the Court of the Imperial Clan.

units.zh: 陰附安樂公主，得稍遷。
units.en: Covertly aligned with Princess Anle, he gradually rose in rank.
units.literal: Covertly attached to Princess Anle, he gradually advanced.

units.zh: 神龍中，鄭普思納女後宮，日用劾奏，中宗初不省，廷爭切至，普思由是得罪。
units.en: During Shenlong, Zheng Pusi sent his daughter into the inner palace; Riyong impeached him; Zhongzong at first ignored the charge, but after fierce debate at court Pusi was punished.
units.literal: During Shenlong, Zheng Pusi presented his daughter to the inner palace; Riyong impeached him; at first Zhongzong paid no heed, but after heated debate at court Pusi was punished on that account.

units.zh: 時諸武若三思、延秀及楚客等權寵交煽，日用多所結納，驟拜兵部侍郎。
units.en: At that time Wu Sansi, Wu Yanxiu, Chuke, and others traded power and favor; Riyong cultivated many alliances and was suddenly made vice minister of war.
units.literal: At that time the various Wu—Sansi, Yanxiu—and Chuke and others exchanged power and favor; Riyong cultivated many ties and was suddenly made vice minister of war.

units.zh: 宴內殿，酒酣，起為《回波舞》，求學士，即詔兼脩文館學士。
units.en: At an inner-palace banquet, when the wine was deep, he rose and danced the "Wave-Returning Dance," asked to be made a scholar, and was immediately ordered to serve concurrently as a scholar of the Xiuxian Academy.
units.literal: At a banquet in the inner palace, when the wine had gone deep, he rose and performed the "Wave-Returning Dance," sought the title of scholar, and was immediately ordered to serve concurrently as a scholar of the Xiuxian Academy.

units.zh: 帝崩，韋後專制，畏禍及，更因僧普潤、道士王曄私謁臨淄王以自托，且密贊大計。
units.en: After the emperor's death, when Empress Wei seized power, he feared for his life and, through the monk Purun and the Daoist Wang Ye, secretly sought out the Prince of Linzi, pledging support for the coup.
units.literal: When the emperor died and Empress Wei monopolized power, fearing calamity would reach him, he further through the monk Purun and the Daoist Wang Ye paid a private visit to the Prince of Linzi to attach himself, and secretly supported the great plan.

units.zh: 王曰：「謀非計身，直紓親難爾。」
units.en: The prince replied, "This is not scheming for myself, only to save my father."
units.literal: The prince said, "The plan is not calculated for one's person; it is simply to relieve a parent's distress.

units.zh: 日用曰：「至孝動天，舉無不克。
units.en: Riyong said, "Filial devotion so great moves Heaven itself—you cannot fail.
units.literal: Riyong said, "Supreme filial piety moves Heaven; in action nothing fails.

units.zh: 然利先發，不則有後憂。」
units.en: But you must strike first, or regret will follow."
units.literal: Yet it profits to strike first; otherwise there will be later worry."

units.zh: 及韋氏平，夜詔權雍州長史，以功授黃門侍郎，參知機務，封齊國公，賜實戶二百。
units.en: After the Wei faction fell, he was named acting chief administrator of Yongzhou the same night; rewarded with the vice-directorship of the Yellow Gate and a share in government, he was created Duke of Qi with two hundred fief households.
units.literal: When the Wei faction was pacified, that night he was ordered to act as chief administrator of Yongzhou; for merit he was made Vice Director of the Yellow Gate with a role in state affairs, enfeoffed as Duke of Qi, and granted two hundred substantive households.

units.zh: 坐與薛稷相忿競，罷政事，為婺州長史。
units.en: A feud with Xue Ji cost him his place at court, and he was sent out as chief administrator of Wu.
units.literal: Because of mutual resentment and rivalry with Xue Ji, he left the government and became chief administrator of Wuzhou.

units.zh: 歷揚、汴、允三州刺史。
units.en: He later served as prefect of Yang, Bian, and Yun in succession.
units.literal: He served in turn as prefect of Yang, Bian, and Yun prefectures.

units.zh: 由荊州長史入奏計，因言：「太平公主逆節有萌，陛下往以宮府討有罪，臣、子勢須謀與力，今據大位，一下制書定矣。」
units.en: Coming in from Jingzhou to report revenues, he said, "Princess Taiping's treason is already showing. You once relied on the palace guard to punish criminals; as prince you needed allies. Now that you sit on the throne, a single edict can finish her."
units.literal: Entering court from chief administrator of Jingzhou to present the annual accounts, he said, "Princess Taiping's rebellious conduct is already sprouting. Your Majesty formerly used the palace offices to punish the guilty; as prince and son, you had to scheme with others for strength. Now that you hold the great position, one imperial decree will settle it.

units.zh: 帝曰：「畏驚太上皇，奈何？」
units.en: The emperor asked, "But I fear frightening my father—what then?"
units.literal: The Emperor said, "I fear alarming the Retired Emperor—what is to be done?"

units.zh: 日用曰：「庶人之孝，承順顏色；
units.en: Riyong answered, "For a common man, filial piety means pleasing a parent's face;
units.literal: Riyong said, "The commoner's filial piety is to comply with his parent's countenance;

units.zh: 天子之孝，惟安國家，定社稷。
units.en: for a Son of Heaven it means securing the realm and fixing the altars of state.
units.literal: the Son of Heaven's filial piety is solely to secure the state and settle the altars of soil and grain.

units.zh: 若令奸宄竊發，以亡大業，可為孝乎？
units.en: If traitors strike and the dynasty falls, is that filial piety?
units.literal: If you allow traitors to steal forth and thereby lose the great enterprise, can that be called filial piety?

units.zh: 請先安北軍而後捕逆黨，於太上皇固無所驚。」
units.en: Secure the Northern Army first, then arrest the rebels—the Retired Emperor need never be troubled."
units.literal: I ask that you first secure the Northern Army and afterward seize the rebel faction; the Retired Emperor will certainly not be alarmed.

units.zh: 帝納之。
units.en: The emperor took his advice.
units.literal: The Emperor accepted this.

units.zh: 及討逆，詔權檢校雍州長史，以功益封二百戶，進吏部尚書。
units.en: During the purge he was again made acting chief administrator of Yongzhou; rewarded with two hundred additional fief households, he was promoted to Minister of Personnel.
units.literal: When the rebels were suppressed, he was ordered to act as inspecting chief administrator of Yongzhou; for merit his fief was increased by two hundred households and he was advanced to Minister of Personnel.

units.zh: 會帝誕日，日用采《詩》《大》、《小雅》二十篇及司馬相如《封禪書》獻之，借以諷諭，且勸告成事。
units.en: On the emperor's birthday Riyong presented twenty odes from the Major and Minor Odes and Sima Xiangru's Letter on the Feng and Shan Sacrifices, using them as indirect counsel and urging him to finish what he had begun.
units.literal: On the Emperor's birthday Riyong selected twenty pieces from the Major and Minor Odes of the Book of Poetry and Sima Xiangru's Letter on the Feng and Shan Sacrifices and presented them, using them to admonish indirectly and also urging completion of the great undertaking.

units.zh: 有詔賜衣一副、物五十段，以示無言不酬之義。
units.en: An edict rewarded him with a suit of robes and fifty lengths of silk, honoring the principle that good counsel deserves reply.
units.literal: An edict granted him one suit of garments and fifty lengths of goods, to show the principle that no words go unrewarded.

units.zh: 久之，坐兄累，出為常州刺史。
units.en: Later, implicated by his brother's troubles, he was sent out as prefect of Chang.
units.literal: After a long while, implicated through his elder brother, he went out as prefect of Changzhou.

units.zh: 後以例減封戶三百，徙汝州。
units.en: By regulation his fief was later cut by three hundred households and he was transferred to Ru.
units.literal: Later, by regulation his fief households were reduced by three hundred and he was moved to Ruzhou.

units.zh: 開元七年，詔曰：「唐元之際，日用實贊大謀，功多不宜減封，復食二百戶。」
units.en: In Kaiyuan 7 an edict declared: "At the dynasty's founding Riyong truly helped shape the coup; his service was too great for a reduced fief—restore two hundred households."
units.literal: In the seventh year of Kaiyuan an edict said: "At the founding of Tang, Riyong truly aided the great plan; his merit was great and his fief ought not to have been reduced—let him again receive two hundred households.

units.zh: 徙並州長史，卒年五十。
units.en: He was moved to chief administrator of Bing and died at fifty.
units.literal: He was transferred to chief administrator of Bingzhou and died at the age of fifty.

units.zh: 並人懷其惠，吏民數百皆縞服送喪。
units.en: The people of Bing mourned him fondly; hundreds of officials and commoners dressed in white and followed his bier.
units.literal: The people of Bing cherished his kindness; several hundred officials and commoners all wore white mourning and escorted the funeral.

units.zh: 贈吏部尚書，謚曰昭。
units.en: He was posthumously honored as Minister of Personnel with the title Zhao (Illustrious).
units.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Personnel, with the posthumous title Zhao.

units.zh: 再贈荊州大都督。
units.en: Later he was posthumously made Grand Protector-General of Jing.
units.literal: He was again posthumously made Grand Protector-General of Jingzhou.

units.zh: 日用才辯絕人，而敏於事，能乘機反禍取富貴。
units.en: Riyong's wit and eloquence were unmatched, he was quick in action, and he knew how to turn danger into rank and riches.
units.literal: Riyong's talent and eloquence surpassed other men, and he was quick in affairs, able to seize the moment, turn calamity back, and obtain wealth and rank.

units.zh: 先天後，求復相，然亦不獲也。
units.en: After Xiantian he sought to regain the chancellorship but never did.
units.literal: After Xiantian he sought to return to the chancellorship, yet he did not obtain it.

units.zh: 嘗謂人曰「吾平生所事，皆適時制變，不專始謀。
units.en: He once said, "Everything I have done in life was to suit the moment and bend with events, not to stick to the first plan.
units.literal: He once told others, "What I have undertaken all my life has been to adapt to the time and control change, not to cling to the first plan.

units.zh: 然每一反思，若芒刺在背」雲。
units.en: Yet every time I look back, it feels like a thorn in my flesh," he said.
units.literal: Yet whenever I reflect on it, it is like a foxtail burr in the back," he said.

units.zh: 子宗之，襲封。
units.en: His son Zongzhi inherited the title.
units.literal: His son Zongzhi inherited the enfeoffment.

units.zh: 亦好學，寬博有風檢，與李白、杜甫以文相知者。
units.en: He too was studious, generous and principled, and counted Li Bai and Du Fu among his literary friends.
units.literal: He too loved learning, was broad and magnanimous with moral bearing, and was known to Li Bai and Du Fu through literary acquaintance.

units.zh: 日用從父兄日知，字子駿，少孤貧，力學，以明經進至兵部員外郎。
units.en: Riyong's cousin Rizhi, styled Zijun, was orphaned in poverty but studied hard and, passing the Classics examination, rose to vice director in the Ministry of War.
units.literal: Riyong's paternal cousin Rizhi, style Zijun, was orphaned young and poor; he studied strenuously and through the Classics examination advanced to Vice Director in the Ministry of War.

units.zh: 與張說同為魏元忠朔方判官，以健吏稱。
units.en: He and Zhang Yue both served as adjutants to Wei Yuanzhong in Shuofang and were known as forceful administrators.
units.literal: He and Zhang Yue alike served as adjutants under Wei Yuanzhong in Shuofang and were known as vigorous officials.

units.zh: 遷洛州司馬，會譙王重福之變，官司逃，日知獨率吏卒助屯營擊賊，以功加銀青光祿大夫。
units.en: Made military adjutant of Luo, he alone rallied clerks and troops when Prince Qiao Chongfu rebelled and officials fled, aiding the garrison against the rebels; for this he received the honorary title Silver-Green Glory Grand Master.
units.literal: He was transferred to military adjutant of Luozhou; when the affair of Prince Qiao Chongfu arose, officials fled, but Rizhi alone led clerks and soldiers to aid the garrison in striking the rebels, and for merit was given the honorary title of Silver-Green Glory Grand Master.

units.zh: 遷殿中少監，建言「廄馬多，請分牧隴右，省關畿芻調」。
units.en: Promoted to junior supervisor of the palace, he proposed, "The stable horses are many; pasture them separately in Longyou to ease fodder levies on the capital region."
units.literal: He was moved to Junior Supervisor of the Palace and memorialized, "The stable horses are many; I ask that they be pastured separately in Longyou to economize on fodder requisitions from the capital region."

units.zh: 授荊州長史，四遷京兆尹，封安平縣侯。
units.en: He served as chief administrator of Jing, rose through four posts to metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, and was created Marquis of Anping.
units.literal: He was appointed chief administrator of Jingzhou, was transferred four times, became Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Anping county.

units.zh: 坐贓，為御史李如璧所劾，貶歙縣丞。
units.en: Convicted of graft and impeached by Censor Li Rubi, he was reduced to assistant magistrate of She.
units.literal: Convicted of corruption, he was impeached by Censor Li Rubi and demoted to assistant magistrate of She county.

units.zh: 後歷殿中監，進中山郡公。
units.en: He later served as palace supervisor and was advanced to Duke of Zhongshan.
units.literal: Later he served as Supervisor of the Palace and was advanced to Duke of Zhongshan commandery.

units.zh: 說執政，薦為御史大夫，帝不許，遂為左羽林大將軍，而自用崔隱甫。
units.en: When Zhang Yue was chancellor he recommended Rizhi for censor-in-chief, but the emperor refused and made Rizhi general of the Left Imperial Insignia Army while appointing Cui Yinpu instead.
units.literal: When Yue held power he recommended Rizhi as Censor-in-Chief; the Emperor did not consent, and Rizhi was instead made General-in-Chief of the Left Imperial Insignia Army, while the Emperor himself employed Cui Yinpu.

units.zh: 隱甫繇是怨說。
units.en: Yinpu hence bore a grudge against Zhang Yue.
units.literal: Yinpu therefore resented Yue.

units.zh: 日知俄授太常卿。
units.en: Rizhi was soon made Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.
units.literal: Rizhi was soon appointed Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.

units.zh: 自以處朝廷久，每入謁，必與尚書齒，時謂「尚書裏行」。
units.en: Having been at court so long, he insisted on taking precedence with the directors at every audience and was nicknamed "the acting director."
units.literal: Considering that he had long been at court, whenever he entered audience he invariably took rank with the Directors—men of the time called him "Director in practice."

units.zh: 終潞州長史，謚曰襄。
units.en: He died as chief administrator of Lu, posthumous title Xiang (Assisting).
units.literal: He ended as chief administrator of Luzhou, with the posthumous title Xiang.

units.zh: 王琚，懷州河內人。
units.en: Wang Ju came from Henei in Huaizhou.
units.literal: Wang Ju was a native of Henei in Huaizhou.

units.zh: 少孤，敏悟有才略，明天文象緯。
units.en: Orphaned in youth, he was quick-witted and strategically gifted, and versed in astronomy.
units.literal: Orphaned young, he was keen and perceptive with talent and stratagem, and understood astronomy and the celestial patterns.

units.zh: 以從父隱客嘗為鳳閣侍郎，故數與貴近交。
units.en: His father's cousin Yin Ke had once been vice director of Phoenix Pavilion, so he moved among the powerful.
units.literal: Because his father's younger cousin Yin Ke had once been Vice Director of Phoenix Pavilion, he often associated with the noble and powerful.

units.zh: 時年甫冠，見駙馬都尉王同皎，同皎器之。
units.en: Still in his teens, he met Commandant-escort Wang Tongjiao, who took a liking to him.
units.literal: At the time he had just reached manhood and met the Commandant-escort Wang Tongjiao, who valued him.

units.zh: 會謀刺武三思，琚義其為，即與周璟、張仲之等共計。
units.en: When a plot formed to kill Wu Sansi, Ju embraced the cause and joined Zhou Jing, Zhang Zhongzhi, and others in planning it.
units.literal: When they plotted to assassinate Wu Sansi, Ju approved their cause and joined Zhou Jing, Zhang Zhongzhi, and others in the plan.

units.zh: 事泄亡命，自傭於揚州富商家，識非庸人，以女嫁之，厚給以貲，琚亦賴以濟。
units.en: After the plot leaked he fled and hired himself to a rich Yangzhou merchant, who saw his quality, married him to his daughter, and supported him handsomely.
units.literal: When the affair was exposed he fled, hiring himself out to a wealthy merchant in Yangzhou; seeing he was no ordinary man, the merchant gave him his daughter in marriage and supplied him generously, and Ju relied on this to get by.

units.zh: 睿宗立，琚自言本末，主人厚賫使還長安。
units.en: At Ruizong's accession he told his full story; his patron sent him back to Chang'an with generous gifts.
units.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, Ju explained his whole story, and his patron richly rewarded him to return to Chang'an.

units.zh: 玄宗為太子，閑遊獵韋、杜間，怠休樹下，琚以儒服見，且請過家，太子許之。
units.en: As crown prince, Xuanzong hunted between Wei and Du; resting under a tree, he met Ju in scholar's robes, who invited him home, and the prince agreed.
units.literal: When Xuanzong was heir apparent he would hunt leisurely between Wei and Du; resting weary under a tree, Ju appeared in scholar's dress, asked to have the prince visit his home, and the prince consented.

units.zh: 至所廬，乃蕭然窶陋。
units.en: At his house the prince found only poverty and squalor.
units.literal: When they reached his dwelling, it was bleak and mean.

units.zh: 坐久，殺牛進酒殊豐厚，太子駭異。
units.en: They sat a long while, then slaughtered an ox and served lavish wine; the prince was astonished.
units.literal: After sitting long, they slaughtered an ox and served wine in unusual abundance; the prince was startled.

units.zh: 自是每到韋、杜，輒止其廬。
units.en: After that, whenever he hunted in Wei and Du, he stopped at Ju's house.
units.literal: From then on, whenever he came to Wei and Du, he would stop at Ju's lodge.

units.zh: 初，太子在潞州，襄城張暐為銅鞮令，性豪殖，喜賓客弋獵事，厚奉太子，數集其家。
units.en: Earlier, while the prince was in Luzhou, Zhang Wei of Xiangcheng, magistrate of Tongdi, was wealthy and loved hunting and guests; he entertained the prince often at his home.
units.literal: Earlier, when the prince was in Luzhou, Zhang Wei of Xiangcheng was magistrate of Tongdi, extravagant and fond of entertaining guests in hunting; he lavishly supported the prince and often gathered at his home.

units.zh: 山東倡人趙元禮有女，善歌舞，得幸太子，止暐第，其後生子瑛者也。
units.en: A Shandong performer named Zhao Yuanli had a daughter who danced and sang; favored by the prince, she stayed at Zhang Wei's house and later bore his son Ying.
units.literal: A Shandong entertainer Zhao Yuanli had a daughter skilled in song and dance who won the prince's favor and lodged at Wei's house; later she bore the son Ying.

units.zh: 太子已平內難，召暐，拜宮門郎，與姜交、崔滌、李令問、王守一、薛伯陽等並侍左右。
units.en: After the internal crisis he recalled Zhang Wei as palace gate officer, with Jiang Jiao, Cui Di, Li Lingwen, Wang Shouyi, Xue Boyang, and others in attendance.
units.literal: After the prince had settled the inner turmoil, he summoned Wei and appointed him Gate Officer of the Palace, with Jiang Jiao, Cui Di, Li Lingwen, Wang Shouyi, Xue Boyang, and others all attending at his side.

units.zh: 令問累擢殿中少監，守一太仆少卿。
units.en: Li Lingwen rose to junior palace supervisor; Wang Shouyi became vice director of the imperial stud.
units.literal: Lingwen was repeatedly promoted to Junior Supervisor of the Palace; Shouyi became Vice Director of the Imperial Stud.

units.zh: 此數人以東宮皆勢重天下。
units.en: Through their ties to the heir apparent, these men all wielded enormous influence.
units.literal: These several men, through the Eastern Palace, all held power weighty under Heaven.

units.zh: 琚是時方補諸暨縣主簿，過謝東宮，至廷中，徐行高視，侍衛何止曰：「太子在！」
units.en: Ju had just become chief clerk of Zhuji and came to thank the heir apparent; in the courtyard he walked slowly, looking about boldly, until an attendant cried, "The crown prince is here!"
units.literal: Ju at this time had just been appointed chief clerk of Zhuji county and came to thank the Eastern Palace; in the courtyard he walked slowly with a high gaze, and an attendant cried, "The crown prince is here!

units.zh: 琚怒曰：「在外惟聞太平公主，不聞有太子。
units.en: Ju snapped, "Out there people talk only of Princess Taiping, not of a crown prince.
units.literal: Ju angrily said, "Outside one hears only of Princess Taiping, not of a crown prince.

units.zh: 太子本有功於社稷，孝於君親，安得此聲？」
units.en: The prince has served the realm and honored his father—how did he come by such a reputation?"
units.literal: The crown prince himself has merit for the altars of state and filial piety toward his sovereign parent—how can such a reputation arise?

units.zh: 太子遽召見，琚曰：「韋氏躬行弒逆，天下動搖，人思李氏，故殿下取之易也。
units.en: The prince summoned him at once; Ju said, "The Wei clan murdered the emperor and shook the realm; men longed for the Li, so you seized power easily.
units.literal: The prince hastily summoned him to audience; Ju said, "The Wei clan personally carried out regicide; the realm was shaken and men yearned for the Li house, so Your Highness took it easily.

units.zh: 今天下已定，太平專思立功，左右大臣多為其用，天子以元妹，能忍其過，臣竊為殿下寒心。」
units.en: Today the realm is settled, but Taiping still schemes for power, many ministers serve her, and the emperor indulges her as his sister—I fear for you."
units.literal: Now the realm is already settled, yet Taiping single-mindedly seeks to build merit; many great ministers at left and right serve her use; the Son of Heaven, as her younger brother by the same mother, can bear her faults—I privately feel cold at heart for Your Highness.

units.zh: 太子命坐，且泣曰：「計將安便？」
units.en: The prince bade him sit and wept, "What is to be done?"
units.literal: The prince ordered him to sit and, weeping, said, "What plan will serve?"

units.zh: 琚曰：「昔漢蓋主供養昭帝，其後與上官桀謀殺霍光，不及天子，而帝猶以大義去之。
units.en: Ju said, "Under Han, Princess Gai raised Emperor Zhao, then plotted with Shangguan Jie against Huo Guang; though she never touched the throne, the emperor removed her on principle.
units.literal: Ju said, "Formerly in Han, Princess Gai raised Emperor Zhao and later joined Shangguan Jie in plotting to kill Huo Guang; she did not reach the Son of Heaven, yet the emperor still removed her on great principle.

units.zh: 今太子功定天下，公主乃敢妄圖，大臣樹黨，有廢立意。
units.en: Your merit has settled the realm, yet the princess plots openly and ministers form factions to replace you.
units.literal: Now the crown prince's merit has settled the realm, yet the princess dares to scheme wantonly; great ministers form factions and there is intent to depose and establish.

units.zh: 太子誠召張說、劉幽求、郭元振等計之，憂可紓也。」
units.en: Summon Zhang Yue, Liu Youqiu, Guo Yuanzhen, and others to counsel you, and your fear may ease."
units.literal: If the crown prince truly summons Zhang Yue, Liu Youqiu, Guo Yuanzhen, and others to plan, the worry can be eased.

units.zh: 太子曰：「先生何以自隱而日與寡人遊？」
units.en: The prince asked, "How can you stay hidden yet visit me every day?"
units.literal: The prince said, "How can you, sir, hide yourself yet day after day keep company with me?"

units.zh: 琚曰：「臣善丹沙，且工諧隱，願比優人。」
units.en: Ju answered, "I know alchemy and merry disguise; let me pass as a court entertainer."
units.literal: Ju said, "Your subject is skilled in cinnabar and also adept at jest and concealment; I wish to be like a performer."

units.zh: 太子喜，恨相知晚。
units.en: The prince was delighted and wished they had met sooner.
units.literal: The prince was pleased and regretted that they had met so late.

units.zh: 翌日授詹事府司直、內供奉，兼崇文學士。
units.en: The next day Ju was made rectifier of the heir's household, inner attendant, and scholar of the Chongwen Institute.
units.literal: The next day he was appointed Rectifier of the Heir Apparent's Household, inner attendant, and concurrently Scholar of the Chongwen Institute.

units.zh: 日以諸王及姜皎等入侍，獨琚常豫秘謀。
units.en: Princes and Jiang Jiao attended daily, but only Ju shared the secret counsel.
units.literal: Day by day the various princes and Jiang Jiao and others entered attendance, but Ju alone was regularly privy to secret plans.

units.zh: 不逾月，遷太子舍人，兼諫議大夫。
units.en: Within a month he became secretary to the heir apparent and remonstrating grandee.
units.literal: Within less than a month he was moved to Secretary of the Heir Apparent and concurrently Remonstrating Grandee.

units.zh: 太子受內禪，擢中書侍郎。
units.en: When the prince took the inner abdication, Ju was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat.
units.literal: When the prince received the inner abdication, Ju was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 公主謀益甚，幽求、暐謀先事誅之，侍御史鄧光賓漏謀，不克，皆得罪。
units.en: As the princess's plots deepened, Youqiu and Zhang Wei planned to strike first, but Censor Deng Guangbin leaked the plot; it failed and all were punished.
units.literal: The princess's plotting grew worse; Youqiu and Wei plotted to act first and execute her, but Attending Censor Deng Guangbin leaked the plan, it did not succeed, and all were punished.

units.zh: 久之，琚見事迫，請帝決策。
units.en: As danger mounted, Ju urged the emperor to act.
units.literal: After a long while, seeing affairs pressing, Ju asked the Emperor to decide.

units.zh: 先天二年七月，乃與岐王、薛王、姜皎、李令問、王毛仲、王守一以鐵騎至承天門。
units.en: In the seventh month of Xiantian 2 he rode with the Princes of Qi and Xue, Jiang Jiao, Li Lingwen, Wang Maozhong, and Wang Shouyi at the head of armored cavalry to the Gate of Accepting Heaven.
units.literal: In the seventh month of the second year of Xiantian, together with the Princes of Qi and Xue, Jiang Jiao, Li Lingwen, Wang Maozhong, and Wang Shouyi, he led iron cavalry to the Gate of Accepting Heaven.

units.zh: 太上皇聞外嘩噪，召郭元振升承天樓，閉關以拒，俄而侍御史任知古召募數百人於朝堂，不得入。
units.en: The retired emperor heard the uproar and sent Guo Yuanzhen to the tower to shut the gates; Censor Ren Zhigu raised hundreds at the court but could not enter.
units.literal: The Retired Emperor heard the outer clamor, summoned Guo Yuanzhen to ascend the Tower of Accepting Heaven, closed the gates to resist; soon Attending Censor Ren Zhigu recruited several hundred men in the court hall but could not enter.

units.zh: 少選，琚從帝至樓下，誅蕭至忠、岑義、竇懷貞，斬常元楷李慈北闕下、賈膺福李猷於內客省。
units.en: Soon Ju followed the emperor below the tower; Xiao Zhizhong, Cen Yi, and Dou Huaizhen were killed, Chang Yuankai and Li Ci beheaded at the northern gate, Jia Yingfu and Li You in the inner service office.
units.literal: Shortly after, Ju followed the Emperor to below the tower; Xiao Zhizhong, Cen Yi, and Dou Huaizhen were executed, Chang Yuankai and Li Ci were beheaded below the northern gate, and Jia Yingfu and Li You at the Inner Service Office.

units.zh: 事平，琚進戶部尚書、封趙國公，皎工部尚書、楚國公，毛仲輔國大將軍、霍國公，守一太常卿、晉國公，各食實戶五百；
units.en: After victory Ju became minister of revenue and Duke of Zhao; Jiang Jiao minister of works and Duke of Chu; Wang Maozhong general who assists the state and Duke of Huo; Wang Shouyi minister of sacrifices and Duke of Jin—each with five hundred fief households;
units.literal: When the affair was settled, Ju was advanced to Minister of Revenue and enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao; Jiao to Minister of Works and Duke of Chu; Maozhong to General Who Assists the State and Duke of Huo; Shouyi to Minister of Imperial Sacrifices and Duke of Jin—each with five hundred substantive households;

units.zh: 令問殿中監、宋國公，實戶三百。
units.en: Li Lingwen became palace supervisor and Duke of Song with three hundred households.
units.literal: Lingwen to Supervisor of the Palace and Duke of Song, with three hundred substantive households.

units.zh: 琚、皎、令問辭不就，以舊官增戶二百。
units.en: Ju, Jiang Jiao, and Li Lingwen declined the new posts and kept their old ranks with two hundred added households.
units.literal: Ju, Jiao, and Lingwen declined and did not accept, keeping their former offices with two hundred additional households.

units.zh: 於是帝召燕內殿，賜金銀雜皿皆一床、帛二千、第一區。
units.en: The emperor feasted them in the inner palace and gave each a couch piled with gold and silver vessels, two thousand lengths of silk, and a mansion.
units.literal: Thereupon the Emperor summoned them to feast in the inner hall and granted gold, silver, and mixed vessels each filling one couch, two thousand lengths of silk, and one fine residence.

units.zh: 帝於琚眷委特異，豫大政事，時號「內宰相」。
units.en: The emperor relied on Ju as on no other, consulting him on great affairs; contemporaries called him the "inner chancellor."
units.literal: The Emperor's trust in Ju was exceptionally singular; he was entrusted with great affairs of state, and men of the time called him the "inner chancellor."

units.zh: 每見閤中，視日薄乃得出。
units.en: Whenever he met the emperor in private, he stayed until sunset.
units.literal: Whenever he was received in the privy chamber, he would not leave until the sun was low.

units.zh: 遇休日，使者至第召之，而皇后亦使尚宮勞琚母，賜賚接足，群臣不能無望。
units.en: On holidays messengers fetched him from home, and the empress sent ladies to honor his mother with endless gifts, to the envy of the court.
units.literal: On rest days, envoys would come to his house to summon him, and the empress also sent palace ladies to comfort Ju's mother, with gifts arriving in succession; the ministers could not be without envy.

units.zh: 或說帝曰：「王琚、麻嗣宗皆譎詭縱橫，可與履危，不可與共安。
units.en: Some told the emperor, "Wang Ju and Ma Sizong are cunning adventurers—useful in crisis, dangerous in peace.
units.literal: Some told the Emperor, "Wang Ju and Ma Sizong are both crafty and unbridled in stratagem; they may be used in danger but not in peace together.

units.zh: 方天下已定，宜益求純樸經術士以自輔。」
units.en: The realm is settled; seek upright scholars for counsel instead."
units.literal: Now that the realm is already settled, you should further seek pure and plain masters of the classics to assist yourself.

units.zh: 帝悟，稍疏之。
units.en: The emperor took the point and drew back from Ju.
units.literal: The Emperor understood and gradually grew distant from him.

units.zh: 俄拜御史大夫，持節巡天兵以北諸軍。
units.en: Soon he was made censor-in-chief and toured the armies north of Tianbing.
units.literal: Soon he was made Censor-in-Chief and, bearing the staff of authority, inspected the armies north of Tianbing.

units.zh: 改紫微侍郎，道未至，拜澤州刺史，削封戶百。
units.en: He was named vice director of the Purple Asterism Bureau, but before arriving was made prefect of Ze and lost one hundred fief households.
units.literal: He was changed to Vice Director of the Purple Asterism Bureau; before he reached his post he was appointed prefect of Zezhou and stripped of one hundred fief households.

units.zh: 歷九刺史，復封戶。
units.en: He served nine terms as prefect and had his fief restored.
units.literal: He served through nine prefectures and had his fief households restored.

units.zh: 又改六州、二郡。
units.en: He later held six prefectures and two commanderies.
units.literal: He was again changed through six prefectures and two commanderies.

units.zh: 琚自以立勛，至天寶時為舊臣，性豪侈，其處方面，去故就新，受饋遺至數百萬，侍兒數十，寶帳備具，闔門三百口。
units.en: Having earned his place among the founding ministers, by Tianbao Ju lived lavishly; in every posting he moved on to fresh appointments, took bribes in the millions, kept dozens of concubines, and maintained a household of three hundred.
units.literal: Ju considered that he had established merit and, by the Tianbao era, was an old minister; he was extravagant by nature, and wherever he served in the regions he left the old for the new, receiving bribes reaching millions, with dozens of serving girls, treasure canopies fully equipped, and three hundred mouths in the whole household.

units.zh: 既失誌，稍自放，不能遵法度。
units.en: Disappointed in his ambitions, he grew reckless and ignored the law.
units.literal: Having lost his ambition, he gradually let himself go and could not observe law and regulation.

units.zh: 在州與官屬小史酋豪飲謔、摴博、藏鉤為樂。
units.en: As prefect he caroused with clerks and local bullies, gambling and playing drinking games.
units.literal: In the prefecture he drank and jested with petty clerks, local chiefs, and strongmen, making sport of dice, pitch-pot, and finger-guessing.

units.zh: 每徙官，車馬數里不絕。
units.en: Each transfer brought a procession of horses and carts miles long.
units.literal: Whenever he was transferred, his carriages and horses stretched for li without end.

units.zh: 從賓客女伎馳弋，凡四十年。
units.en: For forty years he rode out with guests, musicians, and hawks.
units.literal: With guests, female performers, and falconry he galloped and hunted for fully forty years.

units.zh: 李邕故與琚善，皆華首外遷，書疏往復，以譴謫留落為慊。
units.en: Li Yong, his old friend, was likewise exiled in old age; they wrote often, lamenting their fall.
units.literal: Li Yong had long been friendly with Ju; both gray-haired and sent out to the regions, they exchanged letters, taking their censure and banishment as a shared grievance.

units.zh: 右相李林甫恨琚恃功使氣，欲除之，使人劾發琚宿贓，削封階，貶江華員外司馬。
units.en: Li Linfu, resenting Ju's arrogance, had him impeached for old corruption, stripped his rank and fief, and demoted him to assistant magistrate of Jianghua.
units.literal: Chief Minister Li Linfu resented Ju for relying on merit and acting arrogantly and wished to remove him; he had men impeach long-standing corruption, stripped his fief and rank, and demoted him to outer assistant magistrate of Jianghua.

units.zh: 又使羅希奭深按其罪，琚懼，仰藥，未及死，希奭縊之。
units.en: Luo Xiyi pressed the case; Ju took poison, and before it killed him Xiyi strangled him.
units.literal: He further sent Luo Xiyi to press the charges deeply; Ju feared and took poison, but before he died Xiyi strangled him.

units.zh: 時人哀其無罪。
units.en: Contemporaries mourned him as guiltless.
units.literal: Men of the time pitied him as innocent.

units.zh: 始，琚為中書侍郎，母居洛陽，來京師，讓琚曰：「爾家上世皆州縣職，今汝無攻城野戰勞，以謅佞取容，海內切齒，吾恐汝家墳墓無人復掃除也。」
units.en: When Ju was vice director, his mother came from Luoyang and rebuked him: "Our forebears held only local office; you won favor by flattery without battlefield merit—the realm despises you, and I fear no one will tend our graves."
units.literal: At the beginning, when Ju was Vice Director of the Secretariat, his mother lived in Luoyang and came to the capital, reproaching Ju: "Your family's forebears for generations held only prefectural and county posts; now you have no merit of storming cities or fighting in the field, yet by flattery and deceit you win favor—the realm gnashes its teeth at you; I fear your family's graves will have no one to sweep them again.

units.zh: 琚卒不免。
units.en: In the end Ju could not escape her warning.
units.literal: Ju in the end could not escape.

units.zh: 寶應元年，贈太子少保。
units.en: In Baoying 1 he was posthumously made junior tutor to the heir apparent.
units.literal: In the first year of Baoying he was posthumously made Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 太平之誅，張暐召還為大理卿，封鄧國公，實封戶三百，進京兆尹，入侍宴樂，出主京邑，時人以為寵，然自以幹治稱。
units.en: After Princess Taiping's death Zhang Wei returned as director of judicial review, was made Duke of Deng with three hundred households, became metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, feasted in the palace and ruled the capital—an honor, though he was known as an able administrator.
units.literal: When Taiping was executed, Zhang Wei was recalled as Director of the Court of Judicial Review, enfeoffed as Duke of Deng with three hundred substantive households, advanced to Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao, entering to attend banquets and music and going out to head the capital district—men of the time thought it favor, yet he was known for capable administration.

units.zh: 累遷太子詹事，判尚書左右丞，再為羽林大將軍，三至左金吾大將軍，以年高加特進。
units.en: He rose to steward of the heir apparent, judged both wings of the secretariat, twice commanded the imperial guard, thrice the left golden guard, and received special advancement for age.
units.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Steward of the Heir Apparent, concurrently judged the left and right bureaus of the Department of State Affairs, twice became General of the Imperial Insignia Army, thrice Left Golden Guard General, and for advanced age was given special advancement.

units.zh: 子履冰、季良，弟晤，仕皆清近。
units.en: His sons Lubing and Jiliang and his brother Wu all held honored posts.
units.literal: His sons Lubing and Jiliang and his younger brother Wu all held clear and close offices.

units.zh: 暐嘗還鄉上冢，帝賜詩及錦袍繒彩。
units.en: Visiting his ancestral graves, he received an imperial poem and brocade robes.
units.literal: When Wei once returned home to tend the tombs, the Emperor bestowed a poem and brocade robes and colored silks.

units.zh: 乘驲就道，子弟車馬聯咽。
units.en: He traveled by imperial relay; his sons' and brothers' carriages filled the road.
units.literal: He took relay horses on the road; sons and younger brothers' carriages and horses choked the way.

units.zh: 使者賜賚，敕州縣供擬，居處尊顯。
units.en: Imperial gifts followed him, and local officials were ordered to supply his household in splendor.
units.literal: Envoys granted gifts; edicts ordered prefectures and counties to supply his needs; his dwelling and status were exalted.

units.zh: 天寶五載卒，年九十，贈開府儀同三司。
units.en: He died in Tianbao 5 at ninety, posthumously honored as grand master of the palace with the privilege of an opening office.
units.literal: In the fifth year of Tianbao he died, aged ninety, and was posthumously made Grand Master of the Palace with the Honor of Opening an Office.

units.zh: 履冰，歷金吾將軍，季良，殿中監，俱列棨戟。
units.en: Lubing became a golden guard general; Jiliang a palace supervisor; both bore ceremonial halberds.
units.literal: Lubing served as golden guard general; Jiliang as supervisor of the palace; both bore halberd insignia.

units.zh: 王毛仲，高麗人。
units.en: Wang Maozhong was from Goguryeo.
units.literal: Wang Maozhong was a man of Goguryeo.

units.zh: 父坐事，沒為官奴，生毛仲，故長事臨淄王。
units.en: His father was punished and made a government slave; Maozhong was born in bondage and grew up serving the Prince of Linzi.
units.literal: His father was convicted and enslaved to government service; Maozhong was born thereby and so from childhood attended the Prince of Linzi.

units.zh: 王出潞州，有李守德者，為人奴，善騎射，王市得之，並侍左右，而毛仲為明悟。
units.en: Leaving Luzhou, the prince bought Li Shoude, a slave skilled in horsemanship and archery; both attended him, though Maozhong was the sharper.
units.literal: When the prince left Luzhou there was one Li Shoude, a man's slave skilled in riding and archery; the prince purchased him and both attended at his side, while Maozhong was the more perceptive.

units.zh: 景龍中，王還長安，二人常負房箙以從。
units.en: During Jinglong the prince returned to Chang'an; the two often carried his gear.
units.literal: In the Jinglong era the prince returned to Chang'an; the two often carried quivers and followed.

units.zh: 王數引萬騎帥長及豪俊，賜飲食金帛，得其歡心。
units.en: The prince often entertained commanders of the Ten Thousand Riders and bold men with food, drink, gold, and silk.
units.literal: The prince repeatedly summoned commanders of the Ten Thousand Riders and bold men, bestowing food, drink, gold, and silk to win their hearts.

units.zh: 毛仲曉旨，亦布誠結納，王嘉之。
units.en: Maozhong read his mind, won the soldiers over, and won the prince's praise.
units.literal: Maozhong understood his intent and also spread sincerity and formed ties; the prince praised him.

units.zh: 韋後稱制，令韋播、高嵩為羽林將軍，押萬騎，以苛峭樹威。
units.en: When Empress Wei ruled, she put Wei Bo and Gao Song in command of the Ten Thousand Riders and ruled them harshly.
units.literal: When Empress Wei assumed regency she appointed Wei Bo and Gao Song as generals of the Imperial Insignia Army to command the Ten Thousand Riders, establishing authority through harsh severity.

units.zh: 果毅葛福順、陳玄禮訴於王，王方與劉幽求、薛宗簡及利仁府折沖麻嗣宗謀舉大計，幽求諷之，皆願效死，遂入討韋氏。
units.en: Ge Fushun and Chen Xuanli appealed to the prince, who was plotting with Liu Youqiu, Xue Zongjian, and Ma Sizong; all pledged their lives, and they marched against the Wei clan.
units.literal: Company commanders Ge Fushun and Chen Xuanli appealed to the prince; the prince was then planning the great undertaking with Liu Youqiu, Xue Zongjian, and Ma Sizong, adjutant of the Liren Circuit—Youqiu admonished them, and all wished to die in service; they then entered to suppress the Wei faction.

units.zh: 守德從帝止苑中，而毛仲匿不出，事定數日，乃還，不之責，例擢將軍。
units.en: Shoude stayed with the prince in the park; Maozhong hid until days after the coup, yet was not blamed and was promoted to general.
units.literal: Shoude followed the emperor and stopped in the park, while Maozhong hid and did not come out; several days after the affair was settled he returned, was not blamed, and by precedent was promoted to general.

units.zh: 王為皇太子，以毛仲知東宮馬駝鷹狗等坊。
units.en: As crown prince, the prince put Maozhong in charge of the heir's stables, hawks, and hounds.
units.literal: When the prince became crown prince, Maozhong was put in charge of the Eastern Palace's horses, camels, falcons, dogs, and other yards.

units.zh: 不旬歲，至大將軍，階三品。
units.en: In less than a year he reached grand general, third rank.
units.literal: Within less than ten months he reached Grand General, third rank.

units.zh: 與誅蕭至忠等，以功進輔國大將軍，檢校內外閑廄，知監牧使，進封霍國公，實封戶五百。
units.en: For helping kill Xiao Zhizhong and others, he was promoted for merit to General Who Assists the State, oversaw the inner and outer imperial stud parks, supervised the commissioner of herds, and was made Duke of Huo with five hundred substantive households.
units.literal: Joining in the execution of Xiao Zhizhong and others, for merit he was advanced to General Who Assists the State, inspecting the inner and outer stud parks, knowing the supervisory commissioner of herds, promoted to Duke of Huo with five hundred substantive households.

units.zh: 與諸王及姜皎等侍禁中，至連榻而坐。
units.en: He attended in the inner palace with the princes and Jiang Jiao, even sharing couches.
units.literal: With the various princes and Jiang Jiao and others he attended within the forbidden quarters, even sitting on connected couches.

units.zh: 帝暫不見，惘惘若有失，見則釋然。
units.en: If the emperor missed him briefly he grew uneasy; when Maozhong appeared he was comforted.
units.literal: When the Emperor briefly did not see him, he was restless as if lost; when he saw him, he was relieved.

units.zh: 開元九年，詔持節為朔方道防禦討擊大使，與左領軍大總管王晙、天兵軍節度使張說、幽州節度使裴伷先等數計事。
units.en: In Kaiyuan 9 he was sent with staff authority to Shuofang and met with Wang Jun, Zhang Yue, and Pei Youxian to plan campaigns.
units.literal: In the ninth year of Kaiyuan an edict ordered him to bear the staff of authority as defense and campaign commissioner of the Shuofang circuit, and with Left Army General-in-Chief Wang Jun, Tianbing military commissioner Zhang Yue, and Youzhou military commissioner Pei Youxian and others he repeatedly planned affairs.

units.zh: 毛仲始見飾擢，頗持法，不避權貴為可喜事。
units.en: At first, newly honored, he enforced the law fearlessly and pleased the emperor.
units.literal: At first, seeing fine promotion, he quite upheld the law and did not avoid the powerful in matters that could please.

units.zh: 兩營萬騎及閑廄官吏憚之無敢犯，雖官田草萊，樵斂不敢欺。
units.en: Riders and stud officials feared him; even on government land none dared steal fodder.
units.literal: The two camps of Ten Thousand Riders and the stud-yard officials all feared him and none dared offend; even official fields and overgrown wastes—woodcutters dared not cheat.

units.zh: 於牧事尤力，娩息不訾。
units.en: He excelled at herd management; foals and calves multiplied beyond count.
units.literal: In herd affairs he was especially forceful; births and increases were beyond counting.

units.zh: 初監馬二十四萬，後乃至四十三萬，牛羊皆數倍。
units.en: Horses under his charge rose from 240,000 to 430,000; cattle and sheep multiplied likewise.
units.literal: At first supervised horses were two hundred forty thousand; later they reached four hundred thirty thousand, and cattle and sheep were several times more.

units.zh: 蒔茼麥、苜蓿千九百頃以禦冬。
units.en: He planted artemisia and alfalfa on 1,900 qing for winter fodder.
units.literal: He planted artemisia and alfalfa on one thousand nine hundred qing to guard against winter.

units.zh: 市死畜，售絹八萬。
units.en: Dead stock was sold for eighty thousand strings' worth of silk.
units.literal: He purchased dead livestock and sold silk worth eighty thousand.

units.zh: 募嚴道僰僮千口為牧圉。
units.en: He recruited a thousand Yi herders from Yandao.
units.literal: He recruited a thousand Yi boys from Yandao to serve as herdsmen.

units.zh: 檢勒芻菽無漏隱，歲贏數萬石。
units.en: He audited fodder so tightly that yearly surpluses reached tens of thousands of piculs.
units.literal: He inspected fodder and grain without leakage or concealment; each year the surplus reached tens of thousands of piculs.

units.zh: 從帝東封，取牧馬數萬匹，每色一隊，相間如錦繡，天子才之。
units.en: At the eastern Feng rites he paraded tens of thousands of horses in color-ranked companies like brocade, to the emperor's delight.
units.literal: Following the emperor on the eastern Feng sacrifice, he took tens of thousands of herd horses, each color in one company, alternating like brocade; the Son of Heaven was pleased with them.

units.zh: 還，加開府儀同三司，自開元後，唯王仁皎、姚崇、宋璟及毛仲得之。
units.en: On his return he received the privilege of an opening office—after Kaiyuan only Wang Renjiao, Yao Chong, Song Jing, and Maozhong had held it.
units.literal: On return he was given the honor of Grand Master of the Palace with Opening an Office; after Kaiyuan only Wang Renjiao, Yao Chong, Song Jing, and Maozhong obtained it.

units.zh: 然資小人，誌既滿，不能無驕，遂求為兵部尚書，帝不悅，毛仲鞅鞅。
units.en: But he was a man of low birth; once satisfied he grew proud and sought the ministry of war; the emperor refused and Maozhong sulked.
units.literal: Yet he was by nature a petty man; when his ambition was satisfied he could not be without pride, and he then sought to be Minister of War; the Emperor was displeased, and Maozhong was discontented.

units.zh: 及與葛福順為姻家，而守德及左監門將軍盧龍子唐地文、左右威衛將軍王景耀高廣濟數十人與毛仲相倚杖為奸。
units.en: He married into Ge Fushun's family; Shoude, Left Gate Guardian General Lu Longzi Tang Diwen, the Left and Right Martial Guard generals Wang Jingyao and Gao Guangji, and dozens more relied on Maozhong in wrongdoing.
units.literal: When he allied by marriage with Ge Fushun, while Shoude and Left Gate Guardian General Lu Longzi Tangdiwen, Left and Right Martial Guard generals Wang Jingyao and Gao Guangji, and dozens of others relied on Maozhong and committed wrongs together.

units.zh: 毛仲恃舊，最不法。
units.en: Trusting his early service, Maozhong broke the law most boldly.
units.literal: Maozhong relied on old service and was most lawless.

units.zh: 中使至其家稱詔，毛仲不甚恭，位卑者，或踞見，迕意即侮誶，以氣淩之，直出其上。
units.en: When imperial envoys announced edicts at his home he was barely respectful; to inferiors he sprawled; if crossed he insulted them, acting above his station.
units.literal: When palace envoys came to his home to announce edicts, Maozhong was not very respectful; toward those of lower rank he sometimes sat with legs sprawled; if displeased he would insult and revile them, arrogantly lording over them and going straight above them.

units.zh: 高力士、楊思勖等銜之。
units.en: Gao Lishi, Yang Sixu, and others bore him a grudge.
units.literal: Gao Lishi, Yang Sixu, and others harbored resentment against him.

units.zh: 毛仲有兩妻，其一上所賜，皆有國色。
units.en: Maozhong had two wives, one given by the emperor; both were strikingly beautiful.
units.literal: Maozhong had two wives, one of them bestowed by the emperor; both had beauty fit for a kingdom.

units.zh: 嘗生子，帝命力士就賜，仍授子五品官，還，問曰：「毛仲喜乎？」
units.en: When a son was born the emperor sent Lishi with gifts and made the boy a fifth-rank official; returning, he asked, "Is Maozhong pleased?"
units.literal: Once when a son was born, the emperor ordered Lishi to go and bestow gifts, and also granted the son a fifth-rank office; on returning, he asked, "Is Maozhong pleased?

units.zh: 力士奏：「毛仲熟視臣曰：『是子亦何辱三品官？』」
units.en: Lishi reported, "Maozhong glared at me and said, 'Why would that boy be disgraced with only third rank?'"
units.literal: Lishi memorialized, "Maozhong stared hard at your servant and said, 'How would that child be shamed by a third-rank office?'

units.zh: 帝怒曰：「前毛仲負我，未嘗為意，今以嬰兒顧云云。」
units.en: The emperor raged, "Maozhong has long slighted me, which I overlooked; now he scorns even an infant's honor."
units.literal: The emperor angrily said, "Before, Maozhong wronged me and I never minded it; now he goes on about an infant in this way."

units.zh: 力士等知帝怒，它日，從容曰：「北門奴官皆毛仲所與，不除之，必起大患。」
units.en: Knowing the emperor's wrath, Lishi later said gently, "The northern gate officers are all Maozhong's men; leave them and disaster will follow."
units.literal: Lishi and the others, knowing the emperor's anger, another day said at ease, "The slave officials of the Northern Gate were all given office by Maozhong; if they are not removed, great calamity will surely arise."

units.zh: 後毛仲移書太原索甲仗，少尹嚴挺之以聞，帝恐毛仲遂亂，匿其狀。
units.en: Maozhong later wrote Taiyuan demanding arms; Yan Tingzhi reported it, but the emperor, fearing revolt, suppressed the news.
units.literal: Later Maozhong sent a letter to Taiyuan demanding armor and weapons; Junior Administrator Yan Tingzhi reported it; the emperor feared Maozhong would rebel and concealed the report.

units.zh: 十九年，有詔貶州，福順壁州，守德嚴州，盧龍子唐地文振州，王景耀黨州，高廣濟道州，並為別駕員外置。
units.en: In year 19 Maozhong was demoted; Fushun to Bi, Shoude to Yan, Tangdiwen to Zhen, Wang Jingyao to Dang, Gao Guangji to Dao—all as supernumerary vice-prefects.
units.literal: In the nineteenth year an edict demoted Maozhong; Fushun to Bizhou, Shoude to Yanzhou, Lu Longzi Tangdiwen to Zhenzhou, Wang Jingyao to Dangzhou, Gao Guangji to Daozhou—all as supernumerary vice-prefects.

units.zh: 毛仲四子悉奪官，貶惡地，緣坐數十人。
units.en: All four of Maozhong's sons lost their posts and were sent to harsh exile; dozens were punished by association.
units.literal: Maozhong's four sons were all stripped of office and banished to harsh lands; several tens were implicated by association.

units.zh: 有詔縊毛仲於零陵。
units.en: An edict had Maozhong strangled at Lingling.
units.literal: An edict ordered Maozhong strangled at Lingling.

units.zh: 守德本名宜得，立功乃改今名，位武衛將軍。
units.en: Shoude was born Yide and took his present name after earning merit; he became a general of the martial guard.
units.literal: Shoude's original name was Yide; after establishing merit he changed to the present name and held the post of General of the Martial Guard.

units.zh: 嘗遇故主於道，主走避，守德命左右迎之至第，親上食奉酒，主流汗不敢當。
units.en: He once met his old master on the road; the man fled, but Shoude had him brought to his house, served him food and wine himself, while the master sweated in terror.
units.literal: Once he met his former master on the road; the master ran to avoid him, but Shoude ordered his attendants to welcome him to his house, personally served food and offered wine—the master sweated and did not dare accept.

units.zh: 數日，入奏曰：「臣蒙國恩過分，而故主無寸祿，請解官授之。」
units.en: Days later he told the emperor, "I have been favored beyond desert, yet my old master has no stipend—I beg to yield my post to him."
units.literal: Several days later he entered and memorialized, "Your servant has received the state's favor beyond measure, yet my former master has not a foot of salary; I ask to resign my office and give it to him.

units.zh: 帝嘉其誌，擢為郎將。
units.en: The emperor praised his loyalty and made his former master a commandant.
units.literal: The emperor praised his intent and promoted the former master to Commandant of the Guard.

units.zh: 陳玄禮宿衛宮禁，以淳篤自檢。
units.en: Chen Xuanli long guarded the palace and conducted himself with plain integrity.
units.literal: Chen Xuanli long guarded the palace precincts and restrained himself with plain sincerity.

units.zh: 帝嘗欲幸虢國夫人第，諫曰：「未宣敕，不可輕去就。」
units.en: When the emperor wished to visit the Lady of Guo's mansion, Xuanli warned, "Without a proclaimed edict you must not go lightly."
units.literal: The emperor once wished to visit the mansion of the Lady of Guo; Xuanli remonstrated, "Without an announced edict, one must not lightly go or stay.

units.zh: 帝為止。
units.en: The emperor yielded.
units.literal: The emperor stopped on his account.

units.zh: 後在華清宮，正月望夜，帝將出遊，復諫曰：「宮外曠野無備豫，陛下必出遊，願歸城闕。」
units.en: At Huaqing on the first month's full moon, as the emperor prepared an outing, he again urged, "The grounds outside are unguarded—if you must go out, return to the city."
units.literal: Later at Huaqing Palace, on the full-moon night of the first month, when the emperor was about to go out touring, he again remonstrated, "Outside the palace is open wild without preparations; if Your Majesty must tour, I beg you return to the walled city.

units.zh: 帝不能奪。
units.en: The emperor could not refuse him.
units.literal: The emperor could not overcome him.

units.zh: 安祿山反，謀誅楊國忠闕下，不克，至馬嵬，卒誅之。
units.en: When An Lushan rebelled he tried to kill Yang Guozhong at the gate and failed; at Mawei he finally killed him.
units.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, he plotted to kill Yang Guozhong below the palace gate but did not succeed; at Mawei he finally executed him.

units.zh: 從入蜀。
units.en: He followed the emperor into Shu.
units.literal: He followed in entering Shu.

units.zh: 還，封祭國公。
units.en: After the return he was made Duke of Ji.
units.literal: On return he was enfeoffed as Duke of Ji.

units.zh: 及李輔國遷帝西內，玄禮以老卒。
units.en: When Li Fuguo moved the emperor to the western palace, Xuanli died in old age.
units.literal: When Li Fuguo moved the emperor to the western inner palace, Xuanli died of old age.

units.zh: 贊曰：幽求之謀，紹京之果，日用之智，琚之辯，皆足濟危紓難，方多故時，必資以成功者也。
units.en: The commentator says: Youqiu's plots, Shaojing's boldness, Riyong's wit, and Ju's eloquence all availed in crisis; in troubled times such gifts win the day.
units.literal: The eulogist says: Youqiu's plotting, Shaojing's resolution, Riyong's wisdom, and Ju's eloquence were all sufficient to rescue peril and ease difficulty; in times of many affairs, such men must be relied on for success.

units.zh: 雄邁之才，不用其奇則厭然不滿，誠不可與共治平哉！
units.en: Heroic talents unused grow restless—indeed they cannot share a peaceful reign!
units.literal: Talents of heroic breadth, if their strangeness is not used, are discontented and dissatisfied—truly they cannot jointly govern tranquillity!

units.zh: 姚崇勸不用功臣，宜矣。
units.en: Yao Chong was right to warn against keeping meritorious ministers in power.
units.literal: Yao Chong's counsel not to employ meritorious ministers was fitting.

units.zh: 然待幽求等恨太薄雲。
units.en: Yet he treated Youqiu and the others with rather too little grace.
units.literal: Yet in treating Youqiu and the others he was rather too thin in kindness.

units.zh: 毛仲小人，誌得而驕，不足論已。
units.en: Maozhong was a small man who grew arrogant once satisfied—hardly worth mention.
units.literal: Maozhong was a petty man who, when his ambition was satisfied, grew proud—not worth discussing.
